name: Data Table
summary: A data table is rows and columns where every relationship lives in the markup rather than in anything you can see. Use it for real tabular data, not for layout. Which cell is a header and what the table is called are declared, never drawn — a bold first row is not a header row.
demoNote: Every readout here is written by hand and checked against the real accessibility tree by the spec, so it cannot drift. Everything under Common mistakes is live, and each failing table sits beside a correct one that looks the same.

contract.useWhen: A real table: the caption names it, and it scrolls instead of becoming cards.
keyboard: the scroll wrapper is a stop, so it needs a role and a name (SC 2.1.1)
failureModes: every cell a td, with the header row bolded in CSS
scope=col only, so the column is named and the row is not
overflow-x:auto alone: Chromium hands it a tab stop with no role and no name
a paragraph styled to look like a caption, which names nothing
display:block for cards on mobile, which doubles the announcement through td::before content
a base rule written .ac-table th, .ac-table td — (0,1,1) outranks every single-class modifier
